title: Electrical Machines
summary: Highest-yield EE area after power systems. Transformer tests, losses and efficiency; slip and synchronous speed; DC motor characteristics; synchronous machine V-curves and paralleling.
definitions: Transformer principle
Mutual induction: alternating flux from the primary induces EMF in the secondary.
OC test
LV side energised at rated voltage, HV open → core (iron) loss, R0, X0.
SC test
HV side at reduced voltage with LV shorted, rated current → full-load copper loss, Z_eq, R_eq, X_eq.
Voltage regulation
(V_no-load − V_full-load)/V_full-load × 100. Can be negative at leading pf.
All-day efficiency
kWh output ÷ kWh input over 24 h — key for distribution transformers.
Slip
s = (N_s − N)/N_s — the fraction by which rotor speed lags the rotating field.
Back EMF
EMF induced in a motor armature opposing the supply: E_b = V − I_aR_a.
Synchronous condenser
Over-excited synchronous motor at no load supplying leading VArs for pf correction.
V-curve
Armature current vs field current at constant load for a synchronous motor; minimum at unity pf.
Short-circuit ratio
Field current for rated OC voltage ÷ field current for rated SC current ≈ 1/X_s(pu).
formulas: η = xS cos φ / (xS cos φ + P_i + x²P_cu,fl)
P_cu ∝ I² → at half load = ¼ of full-load Cu loss
P_h ∝ f B_m^1.6,  P_e ∝ f² B_m² t²
E = PΦZN/(60A),  lap A = P, wave A = 2
E_b = V − I_aR_a,  N ∝ E_b/Φ,  T ∝ ΦI_a
Rotor Cu loss = s P_g,  P_mech = (1 − s) P_g
s_m = R2/X2;  T_max independent of R2
facts: Buchholz relay: gas-actuated, in the pipe between main tank and conservator; for oil-immersed transformers (> ~500 kVA).
Breather contains silica gel (blue when dry, pink when saturated) to dry incoming air.
Conservator accommodates oil expansion; laminations reduce eddy loss; silicon steel reduces hysteresis loss.
Transformer rated in kVA because losses depend on V and I, not pf.
DC on a transformer primary → no back EMF → very high current → burnout.
Tap changers are on the HV side (lower current, finer steps).
DC series motor: never start on no load (runs away); best for traction (high starting torque).
DC shunt motor: nearly constant speed.
Swinburne's test: no-load test, not for series motors. Hopkinson's: regenerative back-to-back test.
Single-phase induction motor is not self-starting (pulsating field). Synchronous motor is not self-starting.
Increase alternator excitation on infinite bus → changes reactive power; increase turbine input → changes real power.
Hydro alternators: salient pole, many poles, low speed. Turbo-alternators: cylindrical rotor, 2–4 poles.
Regulation methods: EMF pessimistic, MMF optimistic, ZPF (Potier) most accurate.
Paralleling alternators: equal voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase angle. kVA rating need not be equal.
traps: OC test on LV side, SC test on HV side — not the other way round.
Maximum efficiency is when Cu loss = iron loss, not at full load.
Star–delta starter reduces line current to 1/3 (not 1/√3).
Rotor frequency = s × f (2 Hz at 4% slip), not (1 − s)f.
Weakening field flux of a DC shunt motor INCREASES speed.

examples.q: 20 kVA transformer, iron loss 200 W, full-load Cu loss 500 W. Efficiency at full load, 0.8 pf? At what load is η maximum?
steps: x = √(200/500) = 0.632 → max η at 63.2% of full load

examples.q: 6-pole, 50 Hz induction motor runs at 960 rpm. Find slip and rotor frequency.
220 V DC shunt motor, R_a = 0.5 Ω, I_a = 20 A, 1000 rpm. Speed if I_a rises to 40 A (flux constant)?
